design.rationale: The witness suggests that approximately matched x with u=0 can have different drift after different pulse durations. The candidate memory model represents this with z0 driven by u and decaying at rate p0; the current-state model predicts drift determined only by x and u. Use opposite-sign, unequal-duration pulses, then return both inputs to zero so residual history can be compared at a later common time.
design.claim_under_test: At approximately matched x and u=0, drift depends on the preceding input history in a manner consistent with the fitted decaying input-trace state, rather than only on current x and u.
design.expected_separation: If the trajectories reach sufficiently similar x at the comparison time, the current-state model predicts similar subsequent slopes. The memory model predicts different slopes when the residual z0 values differ; the sign and magnitude depend on the fitted contribution of z0 and the histories.
design.failure_of_design: The chosen histories may not yield x values within the matching tolerance at 8 seconds, or their residual memory states may be too similar for a resolvable slope difference. Opposite-sign histories can also leave x on opposite sides of zero, making a useful matched-state comparison unlikely.
